# WrapYourGit

> WrapYourGit turns a developer's GitHub activity for one year into an animated, shareable story: contributions, streaks, languages, top repositories, pull requests and reviews, a developer archetype, a comparison with last year, and a letter from Cell, the mascot. It is free, signs in with GitHub read-only, never reads source code, and every number on screen has a written definition. The current edition is 2026.

Any GitHub username has a recap of its public activity at https://wrapyourgit.habibiahmada.dev/<username>; signing in with GitHub adds your private contribution counts to your own. The story is built from the counts GitHub keeps about your activity; before 31 December it says "so far" and can be synced again. Private repositories count toward totals but are never named in anything that can be shared.

## Pages

- [Home](https://wrapyourgit.habibiahmada.dev/): what the recap contains, the nine chapters, the archetypes, what you can download, privacy facts and the FAQ
- [Privacy policy](https://wrapyourgit.habibiahmada.dev/privacy): what is read from GitHub, what is stored, what goes public and how to delete it

Recaps live at /<github-username>. Every username has one unless its owner hid it, so they are not listed here; each recap page is marked noindex.

## Details

- [Full description for language models](https://wrapyourgit.habibiahmada.dev/llms-full.txt): features, how the numbers are computed, privacy, downloads and FAQ in one file
